chief_complaint: evaluation of shoulder function 3 months post-cuff repair
hpi_details: A 59-year-old male presents for scheduled assessment of shoulder function three months after rotator cuff repair. He wants to review range of motion, strength, and progress with postoperative rehabilitation.
ideas: thinks the symptoms may be related to recovery after rotator cuff repair
concerns: He is worried he will never regain enough overhead reach to return to his job in construction.
expectations: He hopes the doctor will clear him to start lifting light weights and give him a clear timeline for returning to full work.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator Cuff Tear post-rehab evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator Cuff Tear post-rehab is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Postoperative rehabilitation progression must follow the operating surgeon's protocol and repair-specific restrictions. Assess pain, range of motion, strength, wound status, and function before advancing activity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: evaluation of shoulder function 3 months post-cuff repair

Key HPI features: A 59-year-old male presents for scheduled assessment of shoulder function three months after rotator cuff repair. He wants to review range of motion, strength, and progress with postoperative rehabilitation.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Rotator Cuff Tear post-rehab.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator Cuff Tear post-rehab.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: fever, wound drainage, rapidly increasing pain, or sudden loss of strength after a new injury.
management_principles: Measure recovery and advance range-of-motion and strengthening only within the surgeon's repair-specific protocol.
Contact the operating surgeon promptly for wound concerns, new trauma, sudden loss of strength, or rapidly increasing pain.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.objective: Time since surgery and healing course

How high can you currently raise your arm compared to before surgery?

history.answer: I'm here for my scheduled three-month follow-up after my right shoulder rotator cuff repair surgery to see how my recovery and exercises are coming along.
I had arthroscopic repair surgery on my right shoulder exactly three months ago, and my recovery has been steady since then.
The stiffness and mild soreness are right around the top and outside of my right shoulder. It doesn't travel down my arm or up into my neck.
It feels like a dull, mild ache and a tight pulling sensation when I stretch it, about a 2 out of 10. There is no sharp or tearing pain.
It has gradually improved month by month since the surgery, though it tends to stiffen up if I keep it still for a long time.
Reaching high overhead or behind my back brings on the tight ache. Resting the arm and doing my prescribed gentle stretches help ease it.
I haven't noticed any numbness, tingling, swelling, or catching sensations in the shoulder.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, redness, swelling, or any fluid coming from the small surgical scars.
No, I haven't had any falls, sudden pops, sudden loss of arm strength, or sudden severe pain.
I don't have severe night pain anymore and can sleep comfortably on my back or left side, and my weight has been completely steady.
Before the surgery, I had a torn tendon confirmed on an MRI after several months of shoulder pain that didn't get better with therapy.
I place an ice pack on the shoulder for fifteen minutes after my exercise sessions, which helps nicely. I don't take any pain pills anymore.
Nothing specific brings it on except when I reach past my current comfortable range during therapy.
I can do light daily tasks like dressing and grooming with my right arm now, but I still avoid lifting heavy objects or reaching high overhead.
I can raise my arm forward to about shoulder height on my own, but reaching high above my head or behind my lower back is still quite tight.
My strength is slowly coming back for light things, but the shoulder still feels weak if I try to lift anything heavy.
During physical therapy, I feel some stretching tension and mild soreness, but it stays mild and settles down shortly after finishing.
I'm hoping you can check my strength today and give me the green light to start lifting heavier tools again.

history.answer: I assume this stiffness and mild weakness are just a normal part of the healing process after rotator cuff surgery.
I'm terrified that my arm will stay this stiff and I won't be able to get back to my construction job.
I'm hoping you can check my strength today and give me the green light to start lifting heavier tools again.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart disease.
Aside from the shoulder surgery three months ago, the only operation I ever had was an appendectomy when I was in college.
I don't take any prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements right now.
I don't have any allergies to medications, latex, or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I drink one or two beers socially on the weekend, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an office manager doing mostly desk work, and I live with my wife in an apartment.
My father had high blood pressure and passed away in his late seventies, and my mother is eighty-two and in good health.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-developed, comfortable male sitting upright in no acute distress, resting his right arm comfortably.
Small, well-healed arthroscopic portal scars over the right shoulder without redness, swelling, warmth, or drainage.
Active forward elevation to 130 degrees and passive to 150 degrees with end-range tightness, mild anterior subacromial tenderness on palpation, and no joint effusion.
Right shoulder abduction and external rotation strength are grade 4/5 without sudden giving way, and internal rotation and grip strength are 5/5.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation bilaterally over all upper extremity dermatomes, including the lateral deltoid patch.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Full and painless active cervical range of motion without midline neck tenderness or radicular symptoms.
Radial and brachial pulses are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally with capillary refill under two seconds.
